label: karoujite
title: 辛うじて
meaning: barely やっとのことで。何とか。ようやくのことで。わずかに。
meaning_example: I barely made it to the train.

examples.japanese: 走って行ったらかろうじて2時の電車に間に合いました
examples.body_text:
走って行ったらかろうじて2時の電車に間に合いました 

		I ran and 
		barely 
		made the 2 O'Clock train
examples.body_html:
走って行ったらかろうじて2時の電車に間に合いました 
I ran and barely made the 2 O'Clock train

examples.japanese: かろうじて落第せずにすんだ
examples.body_text:
かろうじて落第せずにすんだ 

I just barely 
		managed to avoid dropping out of class
examples.body_html:
かろうじて落第せずにすんだ 
I just barely managed to avoid dropping out of class

examples.japanese: かろうじて付き合っている
examples.body_text:
かろうじて付き合っている 

		They are 
		just barely 
		still together
examples.body_html:
かろうじて付き合っている 
They are just barely still together

examples.japanese: １１時までにかろうじてなんとかその手紙を書いた。
examples.body_text:
１１時までにかろうじてなんとかその手紙を書いた。 

		I barely managed to finish the letter by eleven o'clock.
examples.body_html:
１１時までにかろうじてなんとかその手紙を書いた。  
I barely managed to finish the letter by eleven o'clock.

examples.japanese: かろうじて間に合いましたね。
examples.body_text:
かろうじて間に合いましたね。 

		You are only just in time.
examples.body_html:
かろうじて間に合いましたね。  
You are only just in time.

examples.japanese: かろうじて事故に遭わずにすんだ。
examples.body_text:
かろうじて事故に遭わずにすんだ。 

		I escaped the accident by the skin of my teeth.
examples.body_html:

I escaped the accident by the skin of my teeth.

examples.japanese: かろうじて車に当てられずにすんだ。
examples.body_text:
かろうじて車に当てられずにすんだ。 

		I narrowly escaped being hit by a car.
examples.body_html:

I narrowly escaped being hit by a car.

examples.japanese: かろうじて列車に間に合った。

		I barely managed to catch the train.

comments.text: By the look of the examples, this is spoken grammar?
comments.html: By the look of the examples, this is spoken grammar?

comments.text:
Kaens, I think you mistake 辛 for 幸. 幸 is used in 幸福、幸運 etc.

かろうじて is written as 辛うじて.
comments.html:
Kaens, I think you mistake 辛 for 幸. 幸 is used in 幸福、幸運 etc.
かろうじて is written as 辛うじて.

comments.text:
blabby, this is the grammar for both spoken and written language (of course).

Miki, true, I did mistake that ^^; So, the meaning would be 'bitter, painful, bad' - the opposite to my first comment, so I'm removing that one. Ugh.
